title: A galaxy group candidate at z ≈ 3.7 in the COSMOS field
question: When and where is the earliest maturing phase of galaxy protoclusters and groups taking place, and is HPC1001 a galaxy group at z ≈ 3.7 in the maturing phase?

evidence.quote: we mapped the distance of the fifth neighborhood $\Sigma_{5th}$ for $i$- and $K_s$-detected sources (${\rm S/N}_{i}>5$ & $K_s<25$ AB mag) at $z_{\rm phot}>3$ in the COSMOS2020 catalog (cite: Weaver2022COSMOS2020).
Six of these eight galaxies are also included in the COSMOS2015 catalog (cite: Laigle2016)
HPC1001 was also detected (but barely resolved) in Herschel, SCUBA2 (cite: Simpson2019), and MeerKAT (cite: Jarvis2016mightee) imaging (Fig. 3-left).

recipe.goal: Search for galaxy overdensities at z > 3
recipe.method: Map the distance to the fifth nearest neighbor (Σ_5th) for i- and Ks-detected sources at z_phot > 3 in the COSMOS2020 catalog using GALCLUSTER
key_parameters: S/N_i > 5, K_s < 25 AB mag, z_phot > 3, 5th nearest neighbor

recipe.goal: Measure Optical/NIR photometry, photometric redshifts, and stellar masses of candidate members
recipe.method: Adopt COSMOS2020/Farmer photometry and LEPHARE SED fitting; repeat THE FARMER photometry adding HPC1001.a and h as priors to deblend in Ks and IRAC images
assumptions: Chabrier initial mass function and H0=73, ΩM=0.27, Λ0=0.73 cosmology

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA 1.2 mm continuum and integrated FIR-to-radio photometry
recipe.method: Measure ALMA 1.2 mm continuum using aperture photometry for slightly resolved HPC1001.a and peak fluxes for point-like HPC1001.b, d, and e; measure integrated FIR-to-radio photometry via super-deblending at the fixed position of HPC1001.a
key_parameters: Fixed prior position of HPC1001.a for super-deblending

recipe.goal: Fit FIR-to-radio SED and derive individual and total SFRs, dust masses, and gas fractions
recipe.method: Fit integrated FIR-to-radio photometry with STARDUST using a GN20 starburst template at z=3.7, then split total SFR_IR and M_dust among the four ALMA sources proportional to their ALMA 1.2 mm flux; compute gas mass from dust mass
key_parameters: Redshift fixed at z = 3.7 for integrated SED fit
assumptions: All ALMA-detected sources share the same SED shape as the integrated SED (GN20 template)
Optically thick dust emission in HPC1001.a could overestimate dust mass by a factor of two (included in uncertainty)
Gas-to-dust ratio M_gas = 100 * M_dust with 20% metallicity uncertainty

recipe.goal: Estimate dark matter halo mass and expected baryonic accretion rate
recipe.method: Estimate halo mass using six independent methods (most massive galaxy M_halo-M_* relation, total stellar mass scaling relations from van der Burg+14 and Shuntov+22, X-ray 0.5-2 keV upper limit in 32'' aperture, galaxy number overdensity with bias factor, and extreme value statistics in 2 deg^2), then apply Daddi+2022 scaling relations for BAR and SFR
key_parameters: Completeness limit log(M_*/M_sun) > 9.7 at z=3.7; extrapolation down to 10^7 M_sun; 32'' radius aperture for X-ray; R_vir < 20'', velocity dispersion σ_V = 400 km s^-1, galaxy bias 10-20
assumptions: Field galaxy stellar mass function at 3 < z < 4 (Muzzin+2013); Planck cosmology mean density 7.77e-26 kg m^-3; collapsed structure for virial radius

evidence.quote: HPC1001, which is centered at RA 150.4656$\degree$ and Dec 2.6359$\degree$, is the highest overdensity with $\Sigma_{\rm 5th}$ that is $6.8\sigma$ larger than the mean density of the COSMOS2020 catalog at $z_{\rm phot}>3$.

score_reason: Publicly available catalogs (COSMOS2020, COSMOS2015), public ALMA archival data (2013.1.00034.S), and open-source selection/fitting codes (GALCLUSTER, STARDUST, THE FARMER, LEPHARE) are used, with COSMOS2020 IDs provided in Table 1. However, ALMA imaging/calibration parameters, exact aperture sizes, and the intermediate deblended FIR photometry table are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Both the COSMOS2020 catalog and ALMA archival dataset 2013.1.00034.S are public, the overdensity search code GALCLUSTER is released on GitHub, and key numeric results (1.2 mm fluxes, photo-z, M_*, SFR_IR, M_dust, halo mass) are clearly tabulated.
